c.v: If your picture of public charging is a wallet full of cards, one app per network and a lot of slow posts, it is out of date. This page explains what is different now in Europe and the UK.
All big markets have grown fast. Countries count chargers in different ways, so don't compare the rows with each other. Compare each country with its own past.

rows.v: about 210,000 (public, semi-public and fast), about 3.3 times the roughly 63,000 of 2020
209,605, of which 54,341 fast (above 22 kW in the German definition)

c.v: EV Belgium via The Brussels Times

rows.v: 121,171, of which 28,887 are rapid or faster (50 kW+)

c.v: Across the 27 EU countries there were 1,155,861 public charging points in mid-2026, a preliminary figure from the
Public charging is mainly for longer trips and for people who can't charge where they park. Many owners do most of their charging at home or at work, where it is usually slower and cheaper.
You no longer need an account to charge.

items.v: Every new public charging point of 50 kW or more (built since 13 April 2024) must accept a bank card, through a card reader or a contactless reader. A QR code alone is not enough at these chargers (
Below 50 kW, the operator may offer payment through a QR code and a web page instead. That also works without an account (
From 1 January 2027, older public points of 50 kW or more on the main European road network (TEN-T) must take bank cards too (
The European Commission says a charger where you can only pay in cash does not meet the rules (

c.v: EC questions and answers on AFIR

items.v: All public charge points of 50 kW or more must offer contactless payment, and so must new public points of 8 kW or more installed after 24 November 2024 (
). Operators must also let you pay through at least one roaming provider (

c.v: Do you still want an app or a charging card?

It's optional. A roaming app or card works across many networks. It can be handy where a charger has no card reader, and it can sometimes be cheaper. A subscription is mainly worth it if you fast-charge often. Prices differ by payment method, so check before you choose:
compares the price of a session per card or app.
The price is shown before you start

items.v: the price you pay without a contract is based on the price per kWh. The charger must show it before you start. A fee per minute for staying plugged in may come on top (
the price must be shown before you start too, but it doesn't have to be per kWh. It can be per minute or per session (
the total price must be shown clearly in pence per kWh (

c.v: Fast charging usually costs more per kWh than charging at home. Move the car when it is done, so you don't pay a fee for staying plugged in.
In Europe and the UK, cars sold new today use a

. At a fast charger the cable is attached to the charger, so you don't need your own. Some older used cars, such as the first two generations of the Nissan Leaf, use the older CHAdeMO plug for fast charging instead (
). More on our page about plugs and two-way charging.
Speed: the charger's kW is a ceiling, not a promise
A "150 kW" charger can give up to 150 kW. How much your car takes depends on the car, the battery's charge level and its temperature. The car's
is reached only for a short time. A better guide is the
; our model pages show both. In winter, let the car
on the way to the charger, or charging can be much slower.
Motorways: a fast charger every 60 km on main routes

The EU rules (AFIR) set a minimum for the main European road network (the TEN-T "core" network). Since the end of 2025, there must be a charging site at least every 60 km with at least 400 kW in total and at least one point of 150 kW or more. By the end of 2027 this rises to 600 kW and at least two points of 150 kW or more (
). In June 2026, 79 % of the core network met the 2025 rule, according to an analysis by Transport & Environment (
Many current electric cars plan charging stops in their own navigation and warm up the battery on the way. If you want more control,
plans trips with charging stops for your car.
Chargers do break. In France, 89 % of public points were technically available in the latest 2026 count (
). In the UK, operators must keep their rapid chargers working 99 % of the time on average across their network, and publish the figure (
). Before you rely on one charger, check recent check-ins from other drivers in
, every newly installed or renovated charging point in the EU must support a standard called
. This includes private ones, such as a wallbox at home or at work, for both AC and DC (
It is a language, not a feature.

items.v: ISO 15118-20 is the way the car and the charger talk to each other. It makes two-way charging possible on the software side. It does
mean the wallbox can send power back to your home or the grid. The rules don't make two-way charging or Plug & Charge compulsory (
An installed wallbox doesn't need to be replaced. The rule applies once it is renovated, for example when its technical settings are changed or it gets major repairs (
). There is no date after which a working home charger becomes illegal (
Mode 2 chargers (the cable with a box that goes into a normal socket) don't have to meet this rule (

c.v: Your car must speak it too.

items.v: The new language only helps if the car supports ISO 15118-20 as well. Makers rarely say whether their cars do, and many cars sold up to about 2025 use older versions (
). We show it per car where a source confirms it, and "not disclosed" otherwise.
Testing and certification for ISO 15118-20 are still being set up, so support in practice may be patchy at first (

c.v: Denk je bij openbaar laden nog aan een portemonnee vol laadpassen, een app per netwerk en veel trage palen? Dan is dat beeld verouderd. Op deze pagina lees je wat er nu anders is in Europa en het Verenigd Koninkrijk.
Alle grote markten zijn hard gegroeid. Landen tellen laadpunten op verschillende manieren, dus vergelijk de rijen niet met elkaar. Vergelijk elk land met zijn eigen verleden.

rows.v: ongeveer 210.000 (openbaar, semi-openbaar en snel), zo'n 3,3 keer de ongeveer 63.000 van 2020
209.605, waarvan 54.341 snel (boven 22 kW volgens de Duitse definitie)

c.v: EV Belgium via The Brussels Times
In de 27 EU-landen samen waren er medio 2026 1.155.861 openbare laadpunten, een voorlopig cijfer van het
Openbaar laden is vooral bedoeld voor langere ritten en voor mensen die niet kunnen laden waar ze parkeren. Veel rijders laden het meest thuis of op het werk, waar het meestal trager en goedkoper is.
Je hebt geen account meer nodig om te laden.

items.v: Elk nieuw openbaar laadpunt van 50 kW of meer (gebouwd sinds 13 april 2024) moet een bankpas accepteren, via een kaartlezer of contactloos. Alleen een QR-code is bij deze laders niet genoeg (
Onder 50 kW mag de exploitant ook betalen via een QR-code en een webpagina aanbieden. Ook dat werkt zonder account (
Vanaf 1 januari 2027 moeten ook oudere openbare laadpunten van 50 kW of meer langs het belangrijkste Europese wegennet (TEN-T) een bankpas accepteren (
Volgens de Europese Commissie voldoet een lader waar je alleen contant kunt betalen niet aan de regels (

c.v: vragen en antwoorden van de Europese Commissie over AFIR

items.v: , vraag 5.7).
Alle openbare laadpunten van 50 kW of meer moeten contactloos betalen bieden, net als nieuwe openbare punten van 8 kW of meer die na 24 november 2024 zijn geplaatst (
). Exploitanten moeten je ook laten betalen via minstens één roamingaanbieder (

c.v: Heb je nog een app of laadpas nodig?

Het hoeft niet. Een roaming-app of laadpas werkt bij veel netwerken. Dat is handig waar een lader geen kaartlezer heeft, en soms is het goedkoper. Een abonnement loont vooral als je vaak snellaadt. De prijs verschilt per betaalmanier, dus kijk eerst:
vergelijkt de prijs van een laadsessie per pas of app.
Je ziet de prijs voordat je begint

items.v: de prijs zonder contract is gebaseerd op de prijs per kWh. De lader moet die laten zien voordat je begint. Er kan een bedrag per minuut bijkomen als je aan de lader blijft staan (
ook hier zie je de prijs vooraf, maar die hoeft niet per kWh te zijn. Het kan ook per minuut of per sessie (
de totaalprijs moet duidelijk in pence per kWh worden getoond (

c.v: Snelladen kost per kWh meestal meer dan thuis laden. Zet de auto weg als hij klaar is, dan betaal je geen extra kosten voor blijven staan.
In Europa en het Verenigd Koninkrijk gebruiken nieuwe auto's een

. Bij een snellader zit de kabel vast aan de lader, dus je hebt geen eigen kabel nodig. Sommige oudere tweedehands auto's, zoals de eerste twee generaties van de Nissan Leaf, gebruiken voor snelladen nog de oudere CHAdeMO-stekker (
). Meer daarover op onze pagina over stekkers en tweerichtingsladen.
Snelheid: het vermogen van de lader is een plafond, geen belofte
Een lader van "150 kW" kan tot 150 kW leveren. Hoeveel jouw auto opneemt, hangt af van de auto, hoe vol de accu is en hoe warm hij is. De
haalt de auto maar kort. Beter is de
bereik dat er in 20 minuten bij komt
; beide staan op onze modelpagina's. Laat de auto in de winter onderweg
, anders kan laden veel trager gaan.
Snelweg: om de 60 km een snellader op de hoofdroutes

De EU-regels (AFIR) leggen een minimum vast voor het belangrijkste Europese wegennet (het TEN-T-kernnetwerk). Sinds eind 2025 moet er minstens om de 60 km een laadplein zijn met in totaal minstens 400 kW en minstens één laadpunt van 150 kW of meer. Eind 2027 wordt dat 600 kW en minstens twee punten van 150 kW of meer (
). In juni 2026 voldeed 79 % van het kernnetwerk aan de regel voor 2025, volgens een analyse van Transport & Environment (
Veel huidige elektrische auto's plannen laadstops in hun eigen navigatie en warmen onderweg de accu voor. Wil je meer controle, dan plant
ritten met laadstops voor jouw auto.
Laders gaan weleens stuk. In Frankrijk was in de laatste telling van 2026 89 % van de openbare laadpunten technisch beschikbaar (
). In het Verenigd Koninkrijk moeten exploitanten hun snelladers gemiddeld over hun hele netwerk 99 % van de tijd laten werken, en dat cijfer publiceren (

heet. Dat geldt ook voor privé-laadpunten, zoals een laadpaal (wallbox) thuis of op het werk, zowel AC als DC (
Het is een taal, geen functie.

items.v: ISO 15118-20 is de manier waarop auto en lader met elkaar praten. Het maakt tweerichtingsladen mogelijk aan de softwarekant. Het betekent
dat de laadpaal stroom kan terugleveren aan je huis of het net. De regels maken tweerichtingsladen en Plug & Charge niet verplicht (
Een geplaatste laadpaal hoeft niet vervangen te worden. De regel geldt pas na renovatie, bijvoorbeeld als de technische instellingen veranderen of als er grote reparaties zijn (

items.v: De nieuwe taal helpt alleen als de auto ISO 15118-20 ook ondersteunt. Fabrikanten zeggen zelden of hun auto's dat doen, en veel auto's die tot ongeveer 2025 zijn verkocht, gebruiken oudere versies (

c.v: This page covers two questions buyers ask a lot: "Which plug does this car use?" and "Can this car power my house?". It is about Europe and the UK.
There are only a few plugs to know (

items.v: for
AC charging
at home and at street posts. Every current car in Europe has it.
for
DC fast charging

, an older fast-charging plug. You'll find it on some older used cars, such as the first two generations of the Nissan Leaf, the Nissan e-NV200 and the Mitsubishi Outlander plug-in hybrid. CHAdeMO chargers are getting harder to find.

c.v: Older Tesla Model S and X

items.v: (before 2019) used a modified Type 2 plug at Tesla Superchargers. Teslas sold in Europe now use CCS2.

c.v: When you look at a used car with CHAdeMO, check that there are enough working CHAdeMO chargers on the routes you drive.
"Bidirectional" means the car can give power back, not only take it. There are three levels (

items.v: the car powers a device, such as a kettle, an e-bike charger or camping gear, through a socket or an adapter. Quite common on newer cars.
the car powers your house, for example in the evening or during a power cut. This needs a special wallbox and installation.
the car sends power back to the grid when the grid needs it, and you get paid or get a discount. This needs a special wallbox
an energy contract that supports it.

c.v: V2L is not the same as V2H. A car with a socket for appliances can't power your house just because of that.
Two ways to build it, two price levels
Where the power electronics sit decides what the wallbox costs (

items.v: the car has a two-way charger built in. The wallbox can stay fairly simple. Renault uses this for the Renault 5 and Alpine A290 with its PowerBox Verso wallbox (
the wallbox does the conversion, so it needs much more expensive electronics. Volkswagen's ID. cars use this route with a DC wallbox (

c.v: Only use a wallbox that the carmaker approves for two-way charging with your car.
It depends on where you live
Whether a car can do V2H or V2G for you depends on the country, because energy rules and offers differ.

items.v: had the first commercial V2G offer: the Renault 5 and Alpine A290 with the PowerBox Verso and a Mobilize Power contract, launched in October 2024 (
changed its law in November 2025: power that is stored in a car and later fed back no longer pays grid fees and electricity tax twice. A smart meter is still needed (
). Since then, offers have started. BMW and E.ON sell a V2G package for the new BMW iX3 (from February 2026), with a wallbox, a tariff and a smart meter if you don't have one yet (
). Volkswagen and Elli announced a V2G offer for Germany first, with France and the UK later (
many offers are still pilots or announcements. We show the status per country on each car's page, with the date we last checked.

c.v: Offers change often. Elli, for example, said in November 2026 that it will stop making its own wallboxes and will use a partner's two-way DC wallbox instead (
). We flag facts older than 90 days as "may be out of date".
Buying a used car: check the conditions
For a used car, "can do V2G" often comes with conditions. Volkswagen is a good example (

can charge both ways.
Cars with

On those 3.5 cars, discharging is capped at 10,000 kWh or 4,000 hours in total.
Volkswagen points to its new-car warranty conditions for the rules on two-way charging and the battery.

c.v: So two cars of the same model can give different answers. Ask the seller for:

items.v: the software version,
the battery size, as the
usable (net) capacity
in kWh,
the build date,

c.v: and check the maker's own eligibility page. If a maker doesn't say whether a car supports it, we show "
we don't guess how much two-way charging wears the battery. Read the maker's warranty terms for your car.
From 1 January 2027, every new or renovated wallbox in the EU must support the ISO 15118-20 standard (
). That is the language car and charger use to talk. It makes two-way charging possible on the software side, but it does
make the wallbox two-way: the rules don't require that (
). Your existing wallbox is fine, and your car must support the standard too. More on our page "Charging in 2026: what's changed".

c.v: Electric cars go less far in the cold. That is normal, and it is not a sign of a broken battery. This page explains how much range you lose, why, and what helps.
How much range do you lose?
It depends on the car, the temperature and how you drive. Some numbers from large studies and tests:

items.v: in a study of more than 18,000 cars by Recurrent, the average car kept about
of its range (
). The cars were in the US, compared with their range in mild weather.

c.v: With or without a heat pump:

items.v: in the same study, cars with a heat pump kept about
on average, cars without one about
the results ran from 63 % to 89 % of normal range kept, depending on the model (
in the El Prix test 2025 by the Norwegian motoring club NAF, below freezing, 18 of the 24 new cars ended up 11 % to 23 % short of their
official range
in the El Prix winter test 2026, at temperatures down to −32 °C, the 24 cars fell on average
short of their official range (

c.v: So on a normal winter day, plan for clearly less range than in summer. In a hard frost, or on a fast motorway, the loss can be much bigger.
Heating the cabin uses battery power.

items.v: A petrol car heats with waste heat from its engine. An electric car has very little waste heat, so it uses battery energy to keep you warm.

c.v: A cold battery works less well.

items.v: Cold slows the chemistry inside the cells, so the battery gives less and takes charge more slowly.
winter tyres, wet roads and cold, dense air all add resistance.

c.v: Heating costs energy per hour, not per kilometre. That's why short, slow trips in town lose the most range in percentage terms: you spend a lot of time heating for few kilometres. On a motorway, speed matters more.

Driving faster takes much more energy, in any season. In one test by Bjørn Nyland, a Volkswagen ID.3 used 135 Wh/km at 90 km/h and 205 Wh/km at 120 km/h: about half as much again. Its range fell from 413 km to 271 km (
). Other cars differ, but the direction is always the same. In winter, slowing down a bit on the motorway is one of the easiest ways to get more range.

items.v: It heats the cabin with less energy than a simple electric heater. On many used cars it was an option, so check whether the car you look at has one.

c.v: You'll see "400 V" or "800 V" in car reviews and brochures. It is the
, and it mainly affects how fast a car can charge. For daily driving you won't notice it.

Charging power is voltage times current. With a higher voltage, the car needs less current for the same power. Less current means less heat and thinner cables, so the car can usually charge at high power for longer.
That's the theory. In practice, how fast a car charges depends on the whole car: the battery, its temperature and the software. Look at the
rather than at the voltage or the
We group cars by the battery's
into three classes. The bands are our own simplification, not an official standard (
). Each car's real voltage is also stored and shown, for example 697 V.
Most electric cars on the road so far use a 400 V battery.

items.v: they charge at full speed on almost every
DC fast charger
, old or new, because the charging network was built around them. They are usually cheaper to build.
at very high charging power the current gets very large. That limits how high their top charging speed can go.

c.v: The Porsche Taycan was the first production car with an 800 V system, presented in September 2019 (

items.v: usually faster charging on modern high-power chargers, and less heat.
many older fast chargers only deliver up to about 500 V. On those, an 800 V car must step the voltage up with a
booster
, or it charges at reduced power. On some cars that is much slower than the advertised top speed. Check
"On older chargers"
on the car's page before you buy, especially if your usual routes have older chargers.

c.v: A small but growing group of cars goes even higher:

items.v: Lucid has used what it calls a "900V+" architecture in the Lucid Air (
NIO's ET9 has a drive system that runs at up to 925 V (
BYD presented its Super e-Platform in March 2025, with a 1,000 V architecture and charging power of up to 1,000 kW (
the highest charging power, on chargers that can deliver it.

few chargers outside China can deliver these speeds yet. How these cars behave on older or lower-voltage chargers depends on the car's own converter. Treat claims with care until there are independent tests.

c.v: What this means for a used car

items.v: A 400 V car is the simple choice: it charges well everywhere.
An 800 V car can save time on long trips, if it also charges well on older chargers. Check that before you buy.
For most daily driving, charging at home, voltage makes no difference at all.

Laadvermogen is spanning maal stroom. Bij een hogere spanning heeft de auto minder stroom nodig voor hetzelfde vermogen. Minder stroom betekent minder warmte en dunnere kabels, dus kan de auto meestal langer met hoog vermogen laden.
